newsitem.title: UK: Harrods owners delay flotation plans -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Harrods owners delay flotation plans -- paper.

text.p: Plans to float the world-famous Harrods department store have been delayed by its owners, the al-Fayed brothers, the Financial Times said on Thursday.
The paper said analysts had expected the flotation, which could have valued the group at more than two billion pounds ($3.1 billion), to go ahead early in the autumn.
It would have been supported by a strong international appetite for luxury goods businesses and the successful flotation of Harvey Nichols earlier this year, it said.

The paper said the al-Fayeds were willing to sell up to 20 percent of the London landmark, potentially raising 400 million pounds. It quoted the company as saying: "The Fayeds have checked the engine, dipped the oil and kicked the tyres but have decided they want to keep their beautiful car".

"This has nothing to do with the state of the market or the state of the business. The business is going extraordinarily well," the company is reported to have said. The FT also said expansion plans, including a store revamp and a hotel development, would not be affected.
It quoted one analyst as saying the way the owners wanted to structure the deal may have influenced the decision to delay the float.
